CIVIL JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, KALABURAGI.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
This appeal is by the Corporation questioning quantum determined by the Tribunal in MVC No.643/2019.
2. One Kamalabai succumbed to injuries in a road traffic accident dated 23.03.2015.
Claimants are daughter-in-law and grand children.
A claim petition is filed alleging that Kamalabai prior to accident was working as a helper in Anganawadi Center and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.

Claimants contended that they were totally dependent on the income of the deceased and hence,
filed a claim petition.

The Tribunal in absence of income proof, NC: 2024:KHC-K:9539 however,
proceeded to notionally asses the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- and accordingly, awarded compensation of Rs.5,76,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.6,99,000/-.
3. The appellant/Corporation on receipt of notice tendered appearance and contested the proceedings by filing objections.
In the objection, the Corporation primarily disputed negligence of the driver of the bus.
The Corporation further admitted its liability to pay compensation, but however claimed that the compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.

However, while presenting this appeal before this Court, the Corporation for the first time before this Court contend that daughter- in-law and grand children were not dependent on deceased Kamalabai and therefore,
Corporation is disputing the compensation determined under the head of loss of dependency.
4. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant - Corporation and learned counsel appearing for NC: 2024:KHC-K:9539 respondents - claimants.
Perused the quantum determined by the Tribunal.
This Court has also carefully examined the judgment under challenge.

Managing Director Nekstrc vs Vijaylaxmi W/O Late Basawaraj And Ors on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155729665/
2 5.
Perusal of the judgment under challenge, this Court has noticed that appellant No.1 is the widow of Basawaraj.
Records reveal that Basawaraj has pre- deceased Kamalabai.
Therefore, what can be gathered is that daughter-in-law and two children were residing with Kamalabai.
It is also evident that claimants were residing along with Kamalabai.
On examining the records, this Court is not inclined to accede to the argument that daughter-in-law and grand children cannot assert to be dependents.
The death of Kamalabai obviously affects the claimants and the financial implications are bound to follow on account of death of elderly person in the family.
This Court is also bound to take note of the fact that appellant No.1's husband is also no more.
Therefore, dependency of daughter-in-law and grand children would be more probable on Kamalabai.
Be that as it may.
These grounds were not at all raised while contesting the claim petition.
The Apex Court in catena of judgments has held that dependency varies from case to case and has to be gathered from the facts and circumstances.
The facts in case on hand clearly demonstrate that claimants were obviously dependent on Kamalabai.
In fact, the quantum determined by the Tribunal is very much on the lower side.
The accident is of the year 2015.
Though Tribunal was justified in notionally assessing the income at Rs.8,000/-, future prospects is not added.
The compensation therefore is on the lower side.
Even on this count also, this Court is not inclined to grant any indulgence.
In the light of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birender and Others1, the claimants are legal heirs and therefore they are dependent.

sentences.text: The Tribunal was rightly justified in awarding compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

For the foregoing reasons, this Court passes the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is dismissed.
b) The amount in deposit shall be forthwith remitted to the Tribunal.
c) In view of disposal of main appeal, pending application stands rejected.
Sd/-
